default: It is morning. The grey light comes in as it always does here, from no direction in particular, as though it had been there all along and the dark had only interrupted it.
Pol is up first. She has the fragment and is examining it with the close attention she gives to everything. She is not nervous about it, only thorough.
[missing person] wakes and looks at you, and neither of you needs to say that it is today.
You eat, and you make ready.

default.text: There are Maret's herbs, bitter under your tongue.
There is Edric's ward, cold against your skin.
You have nothing but what [missing person] has told you.

default: And then there is the frame of mind the ritual asks for: to be present, and honest, and not to put on any kind of show. The last is the hardest, and it is what the two days were for.
As you go past, the Watcher at the gate turns a little to watch you, just enough to show that it knows today is different.
text.commander:
You go through the morning as you would before anything that matters. You put aside everything you don't need, and what is left is the task, the method, and the person beside you.

At the mouth of the passage you stop. You are not hesitating. It is only the last moment before you are committed.

"Ready?" [missing person] says.

"Ready," you say.
text.arcane:
You are thinking of the carving on the passage wall, the pictures you read days ago: shut in, breaking, spreading, stopped. The last picture was added lately, by somebody who believed it could be stopped.

You are about to find out whether they were right.

At the mouth of the passage you stop. You can feel the note clearly now, a whole note, and steady.

"Ready?" [missing person] says.

"Yes," you say.
text.ranger:
You go through the morning as you would the last minutes before going into dangerous country, checking what you carry, and what you know, and what you can't know until you are in it.

At the mouth of the passage you look back at Pol, sitting in the outskirts with the fragment and her fifteen years of waiting to be the witness.

"We'll come back," you tell her.

"I know," she says, in the way people say a thing they are not quite sure of but have decided to believe.
text.cipher:
The morning is for getting yourself ready. The ritual is ready already. You are the part that isn't.

You have spent your life showing people only what you meant them to see. The ritual wants something else. It wants you exactly as you are, without any arranging or choosing, without all the careful front you have been building since you were old enough to know that people kept one.

At the mouth of the passage you take a breath, and put it all down.

"Ready," you say.

choices.text: Go into the passage, and walk towards the chamber.

default.text:
You go into the passage.

The carvings close round you. The stone is warm, warmer than last time, as if the mechanism had been working up to something, and today were the day.

You walk the inner approach together, side by side where there is room and one behind the other where there is not. [missing person] goes first in the narrow places, and you follow.

The chamber entrance is ahead. The light beyond it is that wrong light that comes out of the stone, and it is brighter than it was.

choices.text: Sit with [missing person] at the threshold for a while first.

default.text:
You sit on the step at the top of the passage, and they sit beside you. Neither of you says anything worth writing down. Pol waits a little way off with the fragment wrapped in its cloth, and doesn't hurry you.

Then they stand up and hold out a hand, and you go in.

text.default:
The chamber is brighter than before. The light in the stone has grown, not by much, but you can tell, as though the mechanism knew something was coming and had been making ready for it.

The thread rising from the break is stronger too, and easier to see. And it is moving. It no longer simply rises and spreads. It rises and slowly circles, as though looking for something.

[missing person] stops at the place where the text says the first part should begin, and you stop beside them.

"The first part," they say quietly, "is acknowledgement. We say what this place is, what the mechanism was, and what it became when it broke." They pause. "Aloud. The text says aloud. The mechanism reads what we mean, but it is through sound that what we mean reaches it."

They begin.
text.commander:
They speak, and you listen, and then you speak. It is not a prayer. It is a plain statement of what you understand about this place, and what you have come to do.

As you speak, the mechanism does something. The thread from the break turns a little, as if to face you. It is the first sign that whatever is in the ruins knows what is going on in this room.
text.arcane:
This is the part you understand best. It is the theory put into words, the mechanism's first purpose said out loud in front of the mechanism itself.

As you speak, you feel the note change. It grows no louder, but it grows more exact, as though it had found its true pitch again.
text.ranger:
It is simpler than you expected, and more practical than solemn. You say what this place is, and what it does, and what you are going to try to do.

The mechanism is listening. You feel it as you feel being watched when there is nobody to be seen.
text.cipher:
This is the plainest part. You say what you know, and the mechanism reads it and, as far as you can tell, takes it in.

The thread from the break is moving differently now. It is turning towards you, and towards [missing person], as though taking your measure.

choices.text: Finish the acknowledgement, and go on to the engagement.

bonus.label: You know where the ritual text sits

success.text:
The acknowledgement is done. The text said you would know when it was, and the text was right. You feel that you have been heard, and that the mechanism has taken what was said into whatever it is doing.

The thread from the break has settled. It points very slightly towards the two of you, like a compass needle that has found the north.

"The second part," [missing person] says.

success_at_cost.text:
It is heard, but something was not quite right. You stumbled over a word, and for a moment the mechanism's attention seemed to drift and come back. [missing person] notices and carries on smoothly.

"It is all right," they say quietly. "We go on."

failure.text:
It falters. Nothing terrible happens, but the mechanism doesn't answer as the text says it should. [missing person] says, "We step back. We begin again."

You step back to the threshold, and take a breath, and begin again. This time it takes.

text.default:
The engagement is where the ritual reads you.

You and [missing person] take the places the text describes, each in a certain spot in the chamber, facing the mechanism at a certain angle. The fragment is put on the floor halfway between you, touching the stone of the chamber.

It begins at once.

It doesn't hurt, and it doesn't frighten you. What the mechanism does now is not a threat at all. It is the feeling of being seen, entirely: the parts of you that you keep in order, and the parts you keep down, and the parts you haven't looked at straight for years. All of them are equally plain, and equally there, and equally real.

default.text: And it shows you [missing person], the year after you left, standing at the docks on a market day, watching the barges come in. And the next market day, and every market day for a year, in case you were on one.
And it shows you the morning you left. [missing person] is standing in the warehouse door at the docks, watching you go. They did not call out. You never knew they were there.
And it shows you your mother at the end, in the back room on the mill lane, asking for you, and [missing person] holding her hand and telling her you were on your way.
And it shows you [missing person] eleven years ago, reading the old texts by lamplight. They knew already what was under the forest. That was why they sent you away.
And it shows you [missing person] on the pier, watching your barge until it was out of sight. They were proud of you. They have been furious with you for eleven years.
And it shows you [missing person], all those evenings by the mill wall. They knew. They were waiting for you to say it.
There is something you have not told them, and the mechanism finds it first.

default: Across from you, [missing person] is going through the same thing. You can see it in their face, which is the face of somebody being read by something that misses nothing.
text.commander:
You have been in hard places before, where you had to be more than you were, and where everything turned on what you could bring to it.

This is different. This asks you to be exactly what you are, nothing more and nothing added. The mechanism has no use for what you would like to be. It reads what is there.

And what is there, you find, as it reads you, is enough.
text.arcane:
The mechanism reads you completely, all of you at once, in no order and with nothing put first. What you know and what you don't weigh the same with it. What you are clear about and what confuses you, it holds in the same regard.

You have spent your whole working life trying to understand things. The mechanism doesn't understand things as you do. It does not take them apart. It holds them, as the builders held the power, not by understanding it but by giving it something to be.

For the first time you understand what you are doing in this chamber.
text.ranger:
It is not comfortable. It doesn't hurt, but it is complete. You don't get to choose what the mechanism reads. The things you would rather it didn't see are as plain to it as everything else.

But across from you the same is happening to [missing person]. And what you see in their face, as they are read and seen and have nothing kept back, is not that they are less.

It is that somebody else is in the room, and the room can see them.
text.cipher:
The mechanism reads you, and you let it. You could not have done that before the two days of preparing, or before that night by the fire.

You let it read you.

And then something happens that the text never mentioned. The mechanism reads [missing person], across from you, through you. You feel what they are carrying. You don't feel it as yours. You feel it as theirs, coming through the mechanism's reading as light comes through water.

You feel their fourteen months in the ruins, and what they found, and what it cost them, and why they wrote the letter that brought you here. All of it is true.

choices.text: Hold steady, and stay on your feet.

bonus.label: You named it in the ruins

success.text:
You hold. The mechanism reads, and you stay. You don't fight it and you don't put on a show for it. You are simply exactly what you are, at this moment, with this person.

The fragment between you begins to glow, very faintly and very warmly, like something remembering.

"Now," [missing person] says. "We touch. The text says now."

You cross the space between you.

success_at_cost.text:
You hold, but it costs you. The reading goes deep, and down there it finds things you have not looked at for a long time, and to look at them while being looked at takes more than you had expected.

You hold. The fragment glows. [missing person] says, "Now."

You cross the space between you, more slowly than you meant to.

failure.text:
The reading finds something, and you flinch from it. You don't move, but the mechanism reads the flinch as if you had stepped back.

The faint warmth of the fragment flickers.

"[player]," [missing person] says. It isn't one of the words of the ritual. It is your name, which they have known longer than anything else about you, and the sound of it, from them, in this room, reaches you through the flinch and holds you.

You hold. The warmth of the fragment comes back, and the ritual goes on.

choices.text: Stop holding. Let it move through you.

bonus.label: You named it in the ruins

success.text:
You stop holding yourself against it. You let it go through you as water goes through a net, and you stay where you are.

The fragment between you begins to glow, very faintly and very warmly, like something remembering.

"Now," [missing person] says. "We touch. The text says now."

You cross the space between you.

success_at_cost.text:
You let it through, and it takes more with it than you expected. It goes deep, down to things you have not looked at for years, and it takes its time over them.

But you stay. The fragment glows. [missing person] says, "Now."

You cross the space between you, more slowly than you meant to.

failure.text:
You let it through, and for a moment you let go of too much. Something goes out of you that you wanted to keep, and the mechanism feels you going.

The faint warmth of the fragment flickers.

"[player]," [missing person] says. It isn't one of the words of the ritual. It is your name, which they have known longer than anything else about you, and the sound of it, from them, in this room, brings you back.

You stay. The warmth of the fragment comes back, and the ritual goes on.

bonus.label: You named it in the ruins

success.text:
You keep your eyes on [missing person], and whatever the mechanism finds in you, you let it find while you look at them.

The fragment between you begins to glow, very faintly and very warmly, like something remembering.

"Now," [missing person] says. "We touch. The text says now."

You cross the space between you.

success_at_cost.text:
You keep your eyes on them, though it is hard. The reading goes deep, and more than once you want to look away. You don't.

The fragment glows. [missing person] says, "Now."

You cross the space between you, more slowly than you meant to.

failure.text:
The reading finds something, and you look away from them. It is only for a moment, but the mechanism reads it as if you had stepped back.

The faint warmth of the fragment flickers.

"[player]," [missing person] says. It isn't one of the words of the ritual. It is your name, which they have known longer than anything else about you, and you look back at them.

You hold. The warmth of the fragment comes back, and the ritual goes on.

text.default:
You take their hand.

The moment you touch is the moment the mechanism decides.

You feel it before you see it. The chamber changes. The note you have been hearing ever since you came to Ashenveld turns into something else. It resolves, as a held chord resolves when the right note is at last played with it.

The fragment has left the floor. At some point during the reading, without either of you noticing, it rose slowly into the air, and now it glows with a warmth that is also a light. The thread from the break reaches out towards it.

The mechanism knows the fragment. It knows what it was, and it is reaching for what it might be again.
text.commander:
Years of command have taught you to know the moment when a thing is decided, when what was uncertain is certain, and the only question left is not what will happen but what it will cost.

You feel that moment in the chamber now. The mechanism has decided. What remains is the cost.
text.arcane:
The mechanism is not a mind. It doesn't decide things as people do. But it has a purpose, the one it was built for, and when everything is right the purpose works, as a lock works when the right key is turned.

You and [missing person] are the key. The fragment sets it true. The chamber is the lock.

And the lock is turning.
text.ranger:
You hold their hand. The fragment glows. The thread from the break reaches out.

You have tracked many things back to where they came from. This is the first time you have been where something came from.

You hold on.
text.cipher:
The chamber is finishing something. The mechanism's old work, of holding the power by giving it a shape and something to be, is being put back.

The text didn't say what shape it would be given this time. It said that would depend on the two people, on what they are and what they bring.

You hold their hand, and bring everything you have.

choices.text: Hold on, and see it through.

bonus.label: You have listened to it before

success.text:
You hold on.

The mechanism seals.

While it is happening you don't really understand what that means. What you feel is a moment of being entirely here, with nothing at all between you and the room. And then there is a sound, felt and not heard, as something that has been shaking for three years comes true and settles.

The thread from the break vanishes. The fragment goes dark.

The chamber is quiet.

[missing person] is still holding your hand.

success_at_cost.text:
You hold on, and the mechanism seals. But holding on through the whole of the reading has worn you down, and when the sealing is finished you find you are no longer standing. [missing person] is holding you up. They manage it.

The chamber is quiet, and the curse is sealed.

You are going to have to sit down.

failure.text:
You hold on, but not entirely. At the very last something in you fails to give itself, and the mechanism reads it as a gap in what the two of you want.

The seal is only partly made. It is not nothing. The mechanism has answered, the break has narrowed, and the curse will spread far more slowly now. But the whole seal did not take.

When it is over, [missing person] doesn't let go of your hand. "It is enough," they say. "It is not everything, but it is enough. The Covenant cannot do their ritual now the mechanism is partly sealed. They would have to break it open again." They pause. "We have bought Ashenveld time. A good deal of time."

default: After the ritual the chamber is the same chamber, the same stone and the same light and the same size. But the air has changed. The heaviness has gone, and breathing is as breathing ought to be.

default.text: The mechanism in the middle of the chamber is still broken, and the break is still there. The thread coming out of it is thinner, but it is still there. The fragment fell when the sealing ended, and it lies on the floor of the chamber, dark and cool.
default.else: The mechanism in the middle of the chamber is still broken, and the break is still there. But the thread has gone. The fragment fell when the sealing was done, and it lies on the floor of the chamber, dark and cool and quite ordinary.

default: [missing person] sits down beside you on the floor. You are both tired, as people are who have done something that took the whole of them.
You are not the same as you were when you went in. It will take you some time to find out what has changed. But you are here, both of you.
text.commander:
The job is done, and done properly. Those are the facts you start with, whenever something big is over and you have to make sense of it.

But underneath them there is something you couldn't have reached before the ritual. You have been seen entirely and found to be, not perfect, and not simple, but enough.

You will think about that for a long time.
text.arcane:
The mechanism is sealed. You will have to find out what that means for what the curse has already done, to the afflicted people and the animals and the land. Sealing it stops it spreading, but the text did not say whether it would undo the damage.

You have questions, a great many of them, more than you had when you came in. For somebody made as you are, nothing could be better.

And you have something else that is harder to put a name to: what the mechanism showed you of the person beside you, what they carry, why they wrote the letter, and why they waited.

You will think about that for a long time too.
text.ranger:
You look round the chamber as you would look at ground after a storm, for what has changed and what has held.

The mechanism is sealed. The curse can go no further now. What it has done already is another question.

[missing person] is beside you, tired and changed and here.

You have tracked a great many things back to where they came from, and you have not often found what you were looking for when you got there. This time you did.
text.cipher:
The mechanism read you entirely, both of you. You know things about [missing person] now that they did not choose to tell you, and they know things about you.

What to do with that, how to carry it, and what it means for what comes next, is not something the chamber answered. You will have to answer it up above, in the ordinary light.

choices.text: Leave the chamber, find Pol, and go back to the world.

text: You help each other up and leave the chamber together.

The passage is the same passage, and the carvings are the same carvings. But the note you have felt ever since you came to Ashenveld, which began as a pressure in your teeth and became, over the days, as familiar as your own pulse, has changed.

text.text: It is quieter, but not settled. You can still find it if you listen.
text.else: It has not gone, but it has changed. It is quieter. Whatever was shaking has settled.

text: Pol is waiting in the outskirts, at the gate, beside the Watcher. She looks at your faces and knows.

text.text:
"It held," she says. Then: "Mostly."

She doesn't sit down. She stands beside the Watcher with her hands in her sleeves, and you stand with her.
text.else:
"It worked," she says.

"Yes," [missing person] says.

Pol sits down where she stands. She is a very old woman, and her legs have decided that fifteen years of waiting and one morning of witnessing are enough for one day. You sit down beside her.

scenes.title: Too Late or Just in Time

default: You have been sitting with Pol and [missing person] for twenty minutes when you hear people moving in the outskirts.

There is more than one of them. They are Compact soldiers, by the sound, armed men going carefully over ground they don't know. And with them, walking more surely, is somebody who has been here before.
Seriva comes through the outskirts from the west, from the direction of the other way into the inner approach. So she found it.
She stops when she sees you. She looks at the three of you, Pol and [missing person] and you, and at the chamber entrance behind you, and understands what has happened before anyone has said a word.
She doesn't look angry. It is something more complicated than that.

default.text: She walks to the chamber entrance and stands in it for a while. "It is not finished," she says. She is quite right.

text.commander:
There are two soldiers with Seriva. You weigh them up at once: professionals, not looking for trouble, waiting to be told what to do.

Seriva looks at you, and at [missing person], and at Pol, and has worked out everything already.

"The sealing ritual," she says. She isn't asking. She is making sure.

"Yes," you say.
text.arcane:
You think of what Pol told you. Seriva has spent twenty years trying to mend what she broke. The purification was her way of doing it, and she came back to Ashenveld at last to do it.

Now there is no need. The old ritual is done.

What is in her face is grief, very old grief, with a new reason.
text.ranger:
Seriva takes it all in as quickly as an expert would: the chamber entrance, the three of you, and the fragment, dark, on the ground where Pol put it.

She did not come in time. Or else she came only just in time. It depends how you look at it, and what you were hoping for.
text.cipher:
You watch Seriva watching you, and for the first time since you met her she does not quite have herself in hand.

She came here to do a ritual that would have cost Ashenveld a fifth of its people. Now it can't be done. The mechanism has been sealed another way.

She has been let off a duty she has carried for twenty years. She does not look as though she has been let off anything.

choices.text: Tell her what happened, plainly, all of it.

text: She listens without interrupting. When you have finished she is quiet a long while.

text.text:
Then she says, "It will still spread."

"Slowly," [missing person] says. "Years, not weeks."
text.else:
Then she says, "The curse will not spread any further."

"No."

text: "And the afflicted? The people it has already touched?"
"We do not know yet," says [missing person]. "The seal stops it going further. Whether it undoes what has been done, the text did not say."
Seriva nods slowly. Something in her that has been wound tight for twenty years is beginning to loosen. You watch it happen, and it is not comfortable to watch.

"I was going to kill people," she says quietly, to nobody in particular. "I told myself the number was acceptable. I told myself it was necessary. I have told myself so for twenty years, and I believed it, and it was wrong." She pauses. "I am glad it was wrong."

text.text: Then, after a while, she says, "Then my ritual may still be needed."

choices.text: Let Pol speak to Seriva. They have a history.

default.text:
Pol gets up. She is seventy years old, and she has waited fifteen years for this, and she stands up to meet it.

She and Seriva look at each other.

"I was right," Pol says. She doesn't say it as if it pleased her. She says it as somebody does who has been right on her own for a very long time, and is tired.

"Yes," says Seriva.

"The seal is made," says Pol. "The Covenant's ritual can never be done now. It is over."

Seriva looks at the chamber entrance for some time, and then at Pol, and then at the soldiers behind her, who have been standing among ruined buildings trying not to listen.

"Stand down," she tells them. Her voice is not the voice she has used since she came to Crestfall.

choices.text: Use the moment. Seriva needs something from you: your silence about what she did.

success.text:
You see your chance and take it.

Seriva came here to mend the harm she did without anybody ever knowing she had done it. That can't happen now. Pol knows, and [missing person] knows, and you know. The question is whether it goes any further than the people here.

You make her an offer. The Covenant leaves Ashenveld. Seriva gives a full account of the old mechanism to the scholars, for the record. The Rootless camp has the Compact's recognition, and supplies. And in return, what she did twenty years ago stays among the people standing here.

She looks at you a long time. "Yes," she says. "Those terms are acceptable."

It is not a comfortable agreement, but it will hold.

success_at_cost.text: It works, but Seriva insists on one condition: the account she writes will give the credit for the research to the Covenant. You agree. It is a small price for getting the Covenant out.

failure.text:
Seriva will not have it. She is not a woman who takes kindly to being leaned on, and she does not take kindly to it now.

"What I did twenty years ago," she says, "is not yours to trade." She turns to the soldiers. "We are leaving."

She goes with her soldiers, and what she did goes with her, still unsettled.
